description: Provenance for original blog figures. Source repositories were read only. Figures are generated by scripts/generate_figures.py using only the Python standard library.

sources.evidence: The model authors code; the frozen program maps observations to actions without a model-provider call at each step.

The foundation model writes policy.py, executes it, inspects feedback and revises it. Controller logic and a literal PARAMS vector separate code design from numerical search; run_compute uses NumPy/SciPy with no simulator access.
The model writes policy.py with a literal PARAMS list, runs simulation, inspects outcomes and can tune parameters. L3+papers has evaluate_candidates and sandboxed run_compute.

interpretation_limits: This is a method overview, not an execution trace or a quantitative interaction-budget claim.
The tools are optional and differ by experimental treatment.
No real-world robotics demonstration is implied.
method-overview.svg.caption: The foundation model writes a feedback controller, while the frozen program performs control. During learning, simulator feedback guides code revision and optional numerical search. At deployment, state observations pass through the frozen Python policy to native actuator targets without model calls.

adroit-heldout.svg.kind: Original dot-and-interval chart of source report values
adroit-heldout.svg.uncertainty: 95% Wilson interval, copied at the source report's one-decimal percentage precision
interpretation_limits: The intervals quantify uncertainty across held-out seeds for these particular frozen policies, not independent training runs.
These native-reset outcomes do not establish arbitrary physical disturbance robustness.
This campaign has no baseline comparison.
No claim of low simulator interaction cost is supported by this figure.
adroit-heldout.svg.caption: Frozen Adroit policies succeeded on 119 of 120 held-out episodes in the adroit_seq10_l3pr campaign. Each task has 30 unseen starts and one training chain. Points show observed success rates; whiskers show 95% Wilson intervals over held-out seeds for the particular frozen policies.

dexverse-heldout.svg.kind: Original vector chart generated from versioned exact result data
dexverse-heldout.svg.caption: Across 75 valid DexVerse tasks, A0 and L3+papers achieved mean held-out success rates of 94.5% and 94.3%, with unaccepted tasks scored as zero. Each accepted policy was evaluated twice on the same 50 unseen starts; values are averaged across tasks, not independent training runs.
dexverse-heldout.svg.provenance: Source paths, content hashes, definitions, and limitations are recorded in the linked data JSON.

dexverse-search-rollouts.svg.kind: Original vector chart generated from versioned exact result data
dexverse-search-rollouts.svg.caption: Mean search use stayed below 150 rollouts per task in four of six categories for both arms. Counts include recorded parameter-search rollouts only and exclude learning episodes, training evaluations, held-out tests, and uncounted interrupted work. The threshold concerns category means, not all tasks.

adroit-curriculum.svg.kind: Original vector chart generated from versioned exact result data
adroit-curriculum.svg.caption: In these Astra campaigns, final random-reset policies succeeded on more held-out starts than the fixed-start policies. Each task and protocol has one training chain and 30 final test episodes. This is a descriptive comparison: prompts, reset and test seed sets, and actual interaction effort differ, so the contrast does not isolate the causal effect of the curriculum.
